places.name: The chartered-bus pool rules that squeeze a 22:10-22:40 exit
places.note: Give these numbers to the tour agent. A charter registers at the international bus pool, pays ¥2,000 and collects its documents; the pool holds 8 vehicles with a 1-hour cap and the boarding area a 30-MINUTE cap. No advance booking. So the coach cannot idle at the kerb from 21:55: the driver must time pool exit to the group's exit from customs, which for 35 people spreads over 22:10-22:40.

mustSee.title: The 5F rooftop observation deck at 22:30 — the only one open
mustSee.nameJp: 第3ターミナル 屋上展望デッキ
mustSee.summary: Free, landside, and open 開場時間24時間 — the only observation deck at Haneda that is open when this group lands, because T1's and T2's both shut at 22:00 and T2's indoor FLIGHT DECK TOKYO closes at 23:00. A 24-hour deck in a 24-hour terminal is the one genuinely nocturnal sight at this airport, and it is on the same 5F floor the group's Edo Koji record already sends them to. Expect it dim, breezy and lit mainly by apron floodlights.
mustSee.whereToFind: 5F, landside. From the 2F arrival exit take the lifts or escalators up to 5F — the Edo Koji street IS the corridor you walk to reach the deck, so the two frames are one continuous walk, not two stops. Go out onto the roof and walk to the END OF THE DECK FURTHEST FROM THE DOORS you came through, so the apron floodlights are not in your immediate foreground, and shoot from the rail out over the T3 international apron and its gates. CALL 03-5757-8111 BEFORE YOU CLIMB — Haneda's own deck page gives that number and warns 天候や保安上の理由により閉鎖する場合がございます, so with 35 people one phone call saves a wasted lift ride. Assume handheld: no tripod, drone or photography rule is published either way.
mustSee.confidenceNote: The 24-hour opening, the 5F access, the weather-and-security closure warning and the information number are all quoted from Haneda's own deck page and FAQ, and the T1/T2 22:00 closures from the same page. NOT VERIFIED, and deliberately left out of the text above: which compass direction the deck faces, which runway is in view, whether Tokyo Skytree is visible at all, whether the deck is lit at night, and whether it closes for wind specifically. Skytree bears about 012 degrees true at 18.3 km from T3 by calculation from published coordinates — a derived bearing, not an operator statement, and no page confirms the sightline is open. mustSee.title: Edo Koji shuttered at 22:30 — the street with nobody in it
mustSee.summary: The angle the existing facility record leaves on the table: at 22:30 the restaurants are down but the street itself is still public, so the lantern-lit timber shopfronts read as a film set with no diners, no queues and nobody in frame — which is impossible at any other hour of the day. The shutters are the subject, not the limitation. Free, landside, and on the way back down from the deck.
mustSee.whereToFind: Enter at the 4F end of the street and walk it up toward 5F. Shoot DOWN THE LENGTH of the street, camera low and centred between the timber frontages, so the wooden lattice shopfronts and the hanging lanterns converge on the vanishing point — the nihonbashi-style bridge and the two-storey mock-Edo facades only read as a street from a low centred position along the axis; from standing height at the side it reads as a mall. Do the 5F deck first and take this on the way back, because the deck is the half that can be closed by weather.
mustSee.confidenceNote: The facility facts — 4F-5F, restaurants closing about 22:00, the street public at any hour — are already in this bundle's own Edo Koji place record. WHAT IS NOT VERIFIED IS THE LIGHTING: no operator page states whether Edo Koji's lanterns and street lighting stay lit after the tenants close or drop to night levels, and Haneda's 4F and 5F floor-guide pages render no content to a fetcher, so the street's exact position on the floor could not be sourced either. If the lanterns go dark this record collapses to a dim corridor — worth asking on the same 03-5757-8111 call as the deck. Coordinate is Terminal 3's building point, consistent with the postal address 東京都大田区羽田空港2-6-5 shown on the operators' own pages.
